english: A stone coffin rests against the wall.
Of classical dwarven design, used for early Urthfolk tombs.
The lid is sealed tight - almost built into the wall itself.
Symbols of death and rebirth, all dwarven in origin. Forge and hammer.
You run your hand along the stone.
Your eyes trace the symbols carefully.
Typical dwarven work. A few words of poetry. Nothing interesting.
It says, Gudar gâr, folk dôr. Inget nytt under solen.
Along with many other proverbs. Each one personalized for the fallen.
These coffins must have been close dwarven warriors of Urth. Until their graves were exhumed, of course.
It is integrated perfectly into the design.
An iron ring serves as the grip.
A soft click echoes from within the wall.
The handle resists for a moment.
Revealing a narrow staircase descending into darkness.
I'm not feebleminded, if that's what you're asking.
He steels himself and grips his sling.
